## Before you start

- **Designed for:** learners with little or no programming experience.
- **You are ready when:** you can use a web browser and are willing to predict,
  run, explain, and change small examples. No mathematics prerequisite is
  assumed.
- **Practice setup:** start in free Google Colab notebooks. Local Python,
  Jupyter, or VS Code is optional and introduced step by step.

## What you will be able to do

- run Python in a browser and with local tools;
- work with values, text, decisions, loops, and reusable functions;
- choose lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets, and nested data appropriately;
- read tracebacks, inspect program state, and reduce a bug to a useful example;
- build and explain a small working Python project;
- optionally continue into files, environments, testing, typing, OOP, and
  reusable Python patterns before starting a problem-solving course.

## Core curriculum

These five modules and their checkpoints define Foundations curriculum version
1. Complete them in order if you are working toward the local completion record.

::: {.course-grid}
::: {.course-card}
### 1. [Getting Started](getting-started/index.qmd)

Understand how Python runs and choose Colab or local tools for practice.
Two required lessons, one optional local-tools lesson, and one checkpoint.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 2. [Core Python](core-python/index.qmd)

Use values, variables, text, conditions, indentation, loops, and tracing.
Five required lessons and one checkpoint.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 3. [Data Structures](data-structures/index.qmd)

Organize values with lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets, and nested containers.
Five required lessons and one checkpoint.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 4. [Functions](functions/index.qmd)

Package behavior behind clear names, contracts, and focused tests.
Three required lessons and one checkpoint.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 5. [Debugging](debugging/index.qmd)

Read errors calmly and investigate evidence instead of guessing.
Three required lessons and one checkpoint.
:::
:::

## Extended foundations

The following modules were previously labeled Intermediate or Advanced because
they introduce more specialized Python features. They are now optional
Foundations extensions: they deepen your command of the language and its tools,
but they do not change the version 1 completion rule.

::: {.course-grid}
::: {.course-card}
### 6. [Files and Data](files-and-data/index.qmd)

Work safely with paths, external data, exceptions, and validation.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 7. [Projects and Environments](projects-and-environments/index.qmd)

Organize scripts into repeatable projects with dependencies and command-line
entry points.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 8. [Code Quality](code-quality/index.qmd)

Use tests, formatting, linting, typing, pre-commit, and CI to protect behavior.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 9. [Object-Oriented Python](object-oriented-python/index.qmd)

Model data and behavior with classes, dataclasses, composition, and inheritance.
:::

::: {.course-card}
### 10. [Advanced Python Patterns](advanced-python-patterns/index.qmd)

Practice comprehensions, generators, decorators, context managers, logging, and
configuration as reusable parts of your Python foundation.
:::
:::

## Completion requirements and assessment

Python Foundations curriculum version 1 is locally complete when you have:

1. completed all **18 required lessons**;
2. recorded all **five module checkpoints** after meeting their knowledge and
   practical thresholds;
3. built the required [Python Foundations Project](project/index.qmd)
   and self-assessed every rubric row as **Meets the requirement**.

[Local Python Tools](getting-started/local-python-tools.qmd) and all 19 lessons
in Extended Foundations are optional. Completing them is useful preparation for
later applied courses, but they do not change the curriculum version 1 course
status. Lesson quizzes remain formative and do not have a stored grade.

::: {.callout-important title="Local completion is not a verified certificate"}
The completion dashboard is a private, self-reported browser record. It does not
verify identity, submit checkpoint artifacts, grade the project, or issue a
certificate. A verifiable certificate remains planned as a separate service.
:::

## Practice and next step

Every lesson provides runnable examples, practice prompts, a Colab notebook,
and formative quizzes. Each module then asks you to combine those skills in a
practical checkpoint. The final project integrates all five module outcomes.
Extended Foundations can then be studied in any order according to the tools a
learner wants to practice more deeply.
